claim: Framing: for court action too, the amount owed decides what the bank does
source_quote: In a suit for money (including a suit for damages or compensation, or arrears of maintenance, of annuities, or of other sums payable periodically), fee shall be computed on the amount claimed.
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION (framing line; the supporting facts are rows CP-102, CP-111). Court fee is set by the amount claimed (Telangana Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act 1956, s.20) and the DRT route needs 20 lakh or more.

claim: To file a money case the bank must pay court fees (worked out on the amount claimed) and a lawyer
source_quote: In a suit for money (including a suit for damages or compensation, or arrears of maintenance, of annuities, or of other sums payable periodically), fee shall be computed on the amount claimed.
note: Telangana Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act 1956, s.20 and Schedule I Art.1(c). Indian Kanoon flags its copy as not verified against the gazette. Our recomputation of the schedule: Rs 786 on Rs 10,000 (7.9%), Rs 3,426 on Rs 1 lakh (3.4%), matching research_practical 3.1. Fee rates differ by state. Lawyer fees: no source, but the VO gives no figure.

claim: On a small amount court costs eat a big part of what the bank can recover, so a court case for ten thousand rarely makes sense for the bank
source_quote: exceeds one thousand rupees, but does not exceed ten thousand rupees, for every one hundred rupees or part thereof, in excess of one thousand rupees. Seven rupees and fifty naye paise.
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION, labelled on screen (OUR ESTIMATE). Court fee alone is about 7.9% of a Rs 10,000 claim in Telangana (our arithmetic); no bank publishes a minimum amount for suing; research_practical 3.7 found no data on how often banks sue for small card dues.

claim: In one real case SBI Card took card dues of about Rs 1.8 lakh (Rs 1,82,969) to a pre-litigation National Lok Adalat in the customer's own city, Indore (on-screen tag: [MP STATE CONSUMER COMMISSION | 2024])
source_quote: In June 2019, the Company filed a pre-litigation in National Lok Adalat, Indore ... since November 2017, dues of Rs.1,82,969/- as a bill amount, on his credit card is pending
note: M.P. State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bhopal, Appeals 461/2022 and 664/2022, order 28.06.2024: tag name and year are right. The customer's address is Vijay Nagar, Indore. The order does not state the amount in the Lok Adalat filing: Rs 1,82,969 is SBI Card's figure for the bill pending since Nov 2017, and Rs 2,55,662.89 was pending when the account was shown written off (from March 2019). Safer optional wording: 'card dues of more than one point eight lakh'. Spelling: the order body says 'Saji Varghese', the Indian Kanoon title says 'Sajji'.
